q-21222.name: Question 1
q-21222.worked_solution:
First, notice that $△ABC$ is an equilateral triangle. Consequently, all of the interior angles must be equal to ${60}^{∘}:$ 

$$
m∠A=m∠B=m∠ABC={60}^{∘}
$$

Also, since $△CDB$ is an isosceles triangle, the base angles must have equal measure:

$$
m∠CBD=m∠D
$$

Notice also that $∠ACB$ and $∠DCB$ are supplementary, therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠ACB+m∠DCB & ={180}^{∘} \\ {60}^{∘}+m∠DCB & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠DCB & ={120}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

 Finally, we calculate $m∠D$ using the fact that the interior angles of a triangle sum to ${180}^{∘}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠D+m∠DCB+m∠CBD & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠D+{120}^{∘}+m∠D & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2m∠D & ={60}^{∘} \\ m∠D & ={30}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

q-21222.html:
Question 1
?

What is the measure of ∠D?

a
30∘
b
27∘
c
32∘
d
34∘
e
29∘
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that △ABC is an equilateral triangle. Consequently, all of the interior angles must be equal to 60∘:

m∠A=m∠B=m∠ABC=60∘

Also, since △CDB is an isosceles triangle, the base angles must have equal measure:

m∠CBD=m∠D

Notice also that ∠ACB and ∠DCB are supplementary, therefore, we obtain m∠ACB+m∠DCB=180∘60∘+m∠DCB=180∘m∠DCB=120∘.

Finally, we calculate m∠D using the fact that the interior angles of a triangle sum to 180∘: m∠D+m∠DCB+m∠CBD=180∘m∠D+120∘+m∠D=180∘2m∠D=60∘m∠D=30∘

q-21232.name: Question 2
q-21232.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14247769/assets/19ca38571817d9de8c92de17d5121c33ac1494848766033792dc9586c95fa475.png)

In the isosceles triangle $△ABC$  with base $\overset{―}{AB}$, point $E$ lies on the side $\overset{―}{BC}$, $\overset{―}{AE}=\overset{―}{EC}$ and $m∠EAC={40}^{∘}.$ What is the measure of $∠B?$
q-21232.worked_solution:
First, notice that $△ABC$ is an isosceles triangle with base $\overset{―}{AB}.$ Consequently,  the base angles must have equal measure:

$$
m∠BAC=m∠B
$$

Also, since $△CEA$ is an isosceles triangle, we have:

$$
m∠C=m∠EAC={40}^{∘}
$$

Finally, we calculate $m∠B$ using the fact that the interior angles of $△ABC$ sum to ${180}^{∘}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BAC+m∠B+m∠C & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠B+m∠B+{40}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2m∠B & ={140}^{∘} \\ m∠B & ={70}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

In the isosceles triangle △ABC with base AB―, point E lies on the side BC―, AE―=EC― and m∠EAC=40∘. What is the measure of ∠B?

a
67∘
b
69∘
c
72∘
d
70∘
e
73∘
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that △ABC is an isosceles triangle with base AB―. Consequently, the base angles must have equal measure:

m∠BAC=m∠B

Also, since △CEA is an isosceles triangle, we have:

m∠C=m∠EAC=40∘

Finally, we calculate m∠B using the fact that the interior angles of △ABC sum to 180∘: m∠BAC+m∠B+m∠C=180∘m∠B+m∠B+40∘=180∘2m∠B=140∘m∠B=70∘

q-52972.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14247769/assets/372ac1135e480bcd843f02b05bdeae42d462fccaced8151e4a355d6263d7be64.png)

Find the value of $z$ in the triangle shown above.
q-52972.worked_solution:
First, from the diagram, notice that $∠CAB$ and $∠BAD$ are supplementary. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠CAB+m∠BAD & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠CAB+z & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠CAB & ={180}^{∘}-z.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $△ABC$ is an isosceles triangle where $\overset{―}{AB}≅\overset{―}{BC}$, the base angles must be equal:

$$
m∠C=m∠CAB.
$$

Finally, since the interior angles of any triangle sum to ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠CAB+m∠C+m∠B & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2m∠CAB+m∠B & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2({180}^{∘}-z)+{40}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ {360}^{∘}-2z+{40}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2z & ={220}^{∘} \\ z & ={110}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
